summary: This release reads storage version 29, in which a claim's nonce use is kept only as its nonce verdict link and the claim_signature_nonce_uses table and index are gone. The replay check, the seal-time duplicate check and forget's requeue of nonce dependents count a use row or a held claim's nonce link. On a real member the two were the same 3.2 million pairs, so no verdict changes. Nothing in this release drops the table: the writer ships in the next release, and this one is the release it can roll back to. Measured on a copy of a real member, the writer will give back 1.79% of the file, about 340 B per signed claim.

replay.detail: No replay, no scan at open and no background work.

schema.detail: No table, index or column change in this release. Version 29 drops claim_signature_nonce_uses and its key index; this release reads stores with or without them.

rules.detail: Replay rules are unchanged. A nonce use counts only for a claim the store still holds, as before: a forgotten claim lost its use row, and its link, which stays until the link sweep, is not counted. Measured on a copy of a real member: 3,227,325 use rows and 3,227,325 nonce links, equal pair for pair. recheck_claim_verdicts keeps nonce links when it judges every claim again, since from version 29 they may be the only copy of a use. A held claim's nonce link with no use row now counts as a use, as the replay rule intends. Such a link would mean a signature stored before its claim, which no path does today (signatures are stored in their claim's own transaction): on the member copy there were none.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest, capability or synced-table change; nonce uses and verdict links are host-local. Peers of any version are unaffected in both directions.

downtime.detail: None. The replay check adds one primary-key range read of the verdict links per judged signature.

recovery.detail: Roll back to the previous release freely: nothing in this release changes the store.
